summary: Tenant traffic shift caused rapid upstream evictions and short 5xx waves
description:
Issue summary: At ~2026-03-13 19:04 UTC LexaHealth began observing short (~30-120s) waves of 5xx errors for API calls routed to their dedicated pool. Errors manifested as a sawtooth pattern repeating every ~3 minutes. Customer reports spikes started after a traffic routing change from their side (gradual weight shift). Impact: production traffic for a high-availability endpoint experienced elevated error rate and increased latency spikes. Some long-running streaming sessions were dropped.

Environment: prod us-west, LexaHealth dedicated GPU pool (pool-id: lexah-west-01), serving runtime v2.11.2 with kernel-fallback enabled.

Observed behavior: Repeating bursts of 502/503 from api-gateway with concurrent upstream runtime restarts/evictions. Metrics show GPU memory fragmentation followed by runtime worker exits and brief autoscaler cold-starts. Api-gateway logs contain client retry amplification and 5xx queueing.

Expected behavior: Stable request success rate during tenant weight migration; graceful degradation without short oscillatory 5xx waves.

Initial contact: LexaHealth SRE paged support at 2026-03-13 19:10 UTC via #support and opened this ticket.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate a tenant traffic weight shift from backend A -> backend B (20% increments every 30s) while maintaining sustained QPS on the affected endpoint.
2) Observe prefetch activity + KV cache churn for that tenant.
3) Monitor runtime worker memory footprint and kernel fallback metrics.
4) Watch API gateway 502/503 rates and retry amplification.

Notes: Reproduction requires dedicated tenant pool or strong resource isolation to provoke eviction behavior.

2026-03-13 19:22 UTC - Escalated to Runtime SRE (Marco).
2026-03-13 19:30 UTC - SRE hypothesis: tenant prefetch/pinning + rapid weight shift caused KV cache thrash -> worker OOM/evictions -> autoscaler cold starts -> api-gateway retry amplification.
2026-03-13 19:45 UTC - Temporary mitigation: reduced tenant prefetch concurrency and increased autoscaler target buffer for lexah-west-01.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses tested: 
- Hypothesis A: Kernel fallback scheduling on certain sequence-length distributions increases CPU/memory pressure -> confirmed correlated with sequence length p95 spikes.
- Hypothesis B: Autoscaler lag during evictions produces cold-start latency -> supported by scale-up traces showing 20-30s cold windows.
- Hypothesis C: Api-gateway retry policy amplifies transient failures -> observed increased retry_count in gateway logs, leading to additional upstream pressure.

Findings: 
- KV cache lock wait increased concurrently with prefetch bursts for tenant; lock contention correlated with runtime eviction timestamps.
- GPU memory fragmentation (reported by driver metrics) increased after several model-hot-swap events triggered by tenant weight shift.
- Autoscaler configured buffer was minimal for dedicated pools; when 2 workers evicted simultaneously, scale-up lag allowed a short error window.

Evidence links: Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/tenant-ops/lexa-eviction?orgId=1&from=1678797900000&to=1678801500000, Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SUPPORT/p1678799100000
actions_taken:
- Reduced prefetch concurrency for tenant lexah-west-01 from 64 to 12 (config change applied 2026-03-13 19:46 UTC).
- Increased autoscaler target buffer for dedicated pools from 10% -> 30% for lexah-west-01 (applied 2026-03-13 19:48 UTC).
- Temporarily disabled aggressive kernel-fallback path for serving-runtime for this tenant to avoid CPU amplification (feature-flag flip at 19:50 UTC).
- Rate-limited internal retry amplification at api-gateway layer for the tenant to avoid cascaded load (rolled out 19:52 UTC).
- Customer reverted their weight-sweep to a slower cadence while we validated (agreed 19:55 UTC).
resolution:
Partial mitigation achieved: applied config changes reduced error bursts to acceptable levels and customer confirmed stability at 2026-03-13 20:20 UTC.
Final resolution plan: create a postmortem and implement longer-term fixes: automated tenant prefetch throttling during weight shifts, increase default autoscaler buffer for dedicated pools, tenant-level circuit breaker to stop gateway retry amplification, and enhanced eviction monitoring/alerts.
Follow-up tasks (backlog):
- R1: Postmortem doc and action items assigned to Runtime SRE (owner: Marco Nguyen) due 2026-03-20.
- R2: Implement tenant-level cgroup/placement guard to avoid simultaneous evictions (owner: Infra team).
- R3: Add an integration test that simulates weight shift and asserts no >5% error-floor under sustained QPS.

Ticket status: In Progress (waiting on postmortem and engineering follow-ups).
